docs.purpose: The frosted stand-in cards shown to someone whose trial has ended and who dismissed the upgrade screen. It gives the feed and the saved-jobs board a populated shape so they do not look broken, while making clear the content is locked. No real job data is fetched or shown in this state.
docs.data_story: This surface reaches **no API contract at all** — every value it shows is local, passed in as a prop, or read from the device. It holds no client-side store, so there is no local copy of server state to keep in sync. It emits **no analytics event**, so nothing it does is currently countable.
docs.under_126: **RE-PROJECT** — it writes nothing and holds no Layer-3 store, so the move is short — the server already assembles the payload and only the rendering is client-side. It renders through the GATE renderer (a `statuses_handled[]` that must cover every value of the closed set it gates on), reading no contract. Its `owns.components[]` declares `mobile/src/components/paywall/BlurredFeedPlaceholder.tsx`.

contracts: mobile/src/components/paywall/BlurredFeedPlaceholder.tsx:1-57 — renders locked placeholders INSTEAD of issuing /api/leads/feed

identity.owner: unassigned (no CODEOWNERS file and no owner registry exists in the repo — measured 2026-09-15)

versioning.why: One optional `count` prop, two in-repo consumers; a change is one commit.

inputs.why: Only `count` (default 6 for the feed shape, 4 for the board). It deliberately fetches nothing — the user has no entitlement to the data and skipping the request saves the round-trip.

outputs.why: It renders N empty blurred boxes and nothing else.

state.why: No store, no query, no component state.

staleness.why: There is no data to be stale — that is the point of this surface.

session.why: It renders exactly when the user is signed in, subscription_status is expired AND they dismissed the full paywall — the inverse of the entitlement that grants content.

rls_class.why: It reaches no table — and the surface it replaces would have.

checks.why: The lapsed-user branch must NOT issue /api/leads/feed: both parents return before calling the hook, so no lead data crosses the wire to an unentitled device — a blur over real data would be a disclosure defect, not a paywall.
expo-blur silently no-ops on Android below API 31, so the component renders a translucent dark overlay instead; without it the "locked" feel would simply vanish on older devices.
Spec 96 §9 requires at least four placeholders so the screen does not read as broken; the callers pass 6 and 4.

errors.why: No async work and no failure path.

emits.why: The inline-blur state — a lapsed user still opening the app daily — is not instrumented at all.

offers.why: No sponsored placement is rendered: the only slot component in the Expo tree is SponsorSlot, and it returns null unless EXPO_PUBLIC_PARCEL_SPONSORS=1.

metering.why: Nothing here is counted: the Spec 126 §7 usage ledger table does not exist (grep for usage_events in the introspected drizzle schema returns 0 hits), and the only quota-shaped counter, user_profiles.lead_views_count, is incremented solely by POST /api/leads/view, which has no mobile caller.

config.why: The surface consumes no registered logic variable: the only server-side tunable in this path, user_profiles.radius_cap_km, is a per-user admin column, not a logic_variables row.

sharing.why: It renders no contract; it exists precisely to avoid rendering one.

limitations.what: The placeholders are unlabelled and non-interactive, so a screen-reader user in the lapsed state hears nothing at all where the feed used to be.
limitations.measured: grep -c "accessibilityLabel|accessibilityRole" BlurredFeedPlaceholder.tsx → 0; the only copy in the branch comes from the sibling InlineBlurBanner.

notes: InlineBlurBanner — the component that carries the actual explanatory copy in this branch — is rendered by the same two parents but has no census row and no owner (R-13 totality gap).

programme.why: The other product. Inventoried only, fenced by Spec 128 R-03.
